data.title: CBI files chargesheet against Reliance Communications Ltd. (Rcom) in LIC investment fraud case
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 3 -- The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a chargesheet in the Reliance Communications Ltd. (RCom) case before the Special Judge for CBI Cases, Mumbai, against Reliance Communications Ltd., two executives of the Reliance ADA Group, namely, Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, Group MD, Vishwas Joshi, VP, Reliance Capital Limited, and P Venugopal, the then Chief Investment Officer, LIC.

According to an official release, the four accused have been chargesheeted for offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating and criminal breach of trust under the IPC, along with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

Further investigation is continuing to ascertain the role of other accused persons and to investigate other allegations.

According to the press release, the investigation conducted so far has revealed that, in 2012, LIC subscribed to NCDs worth Rs. 1,500 crore issued by Reliance Communications Ltd. based on serious misrepresentations.

The funds received through the NCD subscription were thereafter diverted to ADA group companies, thereby causing wrongful loss to LIC and corresponding wrongful gain to the accused persons and entities.

It may be recalled that the CBI had registered the case on April 1 2026, based on a complaint received from the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The total alleged loss caused to LIC amounts to Rs. 3,750 crore, the release stated.

It may also be recalled that the CBI, BSFB, Delhi, has registered nine FIRs against Reliance Communications Limited (RCom), Reliance Home Finance Limited (RHFL), Reliance Commercial Finance Limited (RCFL), Reliance Telecom Limited (RTL) and other Reliance ADA Group entities based on complaints received from various Public Sector Banks, LIC and EPFO.

The CBI had earlier filed seven chargesheets in the Reliance ADA Group cases. The present chargesheet is the eighth chargesheet filed in these cases, and the CBI has so far arrested seven accused persons.

The investigation in these cases is being monitored by the Supreme Court, and the CBI remains committed to conducting an expeditious and comprehensive investigation into these cases, the release said.

data.title: India widens crude sourcing to 43 countries to boost energy security, says top government official
data.description:
NEW DELHI, Oct. 3 -- India has widened its crude-oil sourcing base to 43 countries from 27 to reduce exposure to geopolitical shocks while remaining integrated with the global economy, said P. K. Mishra, principal secretary to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The diversification reflects a broader approach to economic security, Mishra said at the Kautaliya Economic Conclave 2026 in New Delhi. Resilience, he said, is not about eliminating dependence on other countries, but avoiding excessive concentration in any one source.

"For example, the number of countries from which we import crude oil has increased from 27 to 43," Mishra said, calling the expansion significant for India's energy security.

The strategy assumes importance as India relies on imported crude for nearly 90% of domestic demand, leaving the economy exposed to geopolitical disruptions, shipping risks and swings in global oil prices.

The diversification comes as the West Asia war, which flared up again in August and September, pushed crude prices to nearly $100 a barrel. Before the war, prices were at $65 a barrel.

On Friday, Brent crude on the Intercontinental Exchange ended at $102.25 a barrel. An increase of around $1 a barrel a year could raise India's annual import bill by Rs.18,000 crore, according to estimates by Bank of Baroda.

India imported $123.37 billion worth of crude oil in fiscal year 2026 (FY26), down from $137 billion in the previous year.

Mishra said the larger meaning of 'atmanirbharata' was not an economy that needs no one, but one that can withstand disruption and adapt to change. Wars, trade disruptions, volatile energy prices and artificial intelligence are creating new sources of uncertainty, he said.

"Atmanirbhar Bharat is not about being self-contained or being close to the world. It is about being self-sustaining and self-generating. In a world price at risk, this may ultimately be the most durable form of economic security-not an economy that needs no one, but an economy that can withstand disruption, adapt to change, and create value that the world itself cannot do without," Mishra said.

The same principle applies to critical minerals, energy and manufacturing, Mishra said.

Critical minerals needed for the global energy transition are held in "very few hands", creating the potential for countries to weaponize control over them, he said. India's response is to combine domestic capability where vulnerabilities are strategic, diversification where concentration creates risks and openness where global integration improves productivity and competitiveness.

"Greater domestic capacity in renewables, nuclear energy storage, and associated technologies is not only about sustainability; it is also about reducing exposure to external shocks over time," Mishra said.

The National Critical Minerals Mission is aimed at strengthening domestic exploration, processing and recycling, while India has partnerships with the US, France, Germany and the Netherlands covering exploration, processing, recycling, technology and supply-chain resilience.

Mishra said resilience had to be balanced against efficiency: global supply chains can deliver cost advantages, while concentrated sources can leave economies vulnerable to disruption. Domestic capabilities should therefore be competitive, scalable and eventually export-oriented rather than simply replacing imports.

Electronics illustrates the approach. Production rose from around Rs.2 trillion in FY15 to about Rs.13 trillion in FY26, while exports increased from around Rs.38,000 crore to Rs.4.24 trillion.

The policy focus is also moving beyond assembly towards components and a deeper manufacturing ecosystem, with similar efforts in semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and other strategic sectors.

India has also expanded its trade-agreement network, including with the United Arab Emirates, Australia and EFTA, and more recently the UK, Oman and New Zealand.

"An open economy will always depend on other economies. The objective is not to eliminate that dependence, but to avoid excessive concentration," he said.

Mishra linked resilience to macroeconomic strength, including fiscal space, adequate foreign-exchange reserves, a sound financial system and credible institutions.

India has continued fiscal consolidation while maintaining public investment. The fiscal deficit, which rose to more than 9% of GDP during the pandemic, is budgeted at 4.3% of GDP in FY27.

Resilience comes at a cost, Mishra said: strategic reserves must be financed, alternative suppliers may be more expensive and domestic capacity can initially cost more than imports. But such costs can be justified where disruption carries a large economic and social cost.

"Where a disruption can impose a very large economic and social cost, investing in resilience can be economically rational," Mishra said.

data.title: "Matter of great pride": Rajeev Shukla hails India's Asian Games gold win over Pakistan
data.description:
Meerut, Oct. 3 -- Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Vice-President Rajeev Shukla on Saturday hailed India's Asian Games cricket gold medal win over Pakistan as a matter of great pride, praising the players for adapting to unfamiliar wicket conditions in Japan and delivering a strong performance.

He said the victory reflects the continued growth of Indian cricket under the BCCI, while highlighting the team's recent successes.

India have now won 83 medals - 20 gold, 26 silver and 37 bronze - at the Asian Games 2026 so far.

Shukla also praised India's growing pool of players, saying the depth allows different squads to compete in multiple series and provides opportunities for more players while maintaining a winning run.

Following the women's team's triumph, India's men also defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the gold medal clash at the ongoing Asian Games on Saturday, with stellar performances from Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Varma and Axar Patel powering the team to victory.

"This is a matter of great pride that today we won the gold medal in cricket in the Asian Games by defeating Pakistan, and our players performed very well. If we look at the wicket conditions there, our players were not that familiar with the wicket there. Despite this, they performed very well and reached the final and by defeating Pakistan in the final, we got the gold medal in cricket in the Asian Games once again, so cricket is growing everywhere under the efforts of the BCCI. We have already won the Asia Cup, we have won in the Asian Games too, we have taken the World Cup too, so India's cricket is continuously growing," Shukla told ANI on Saturday in Meerut.

"One special thing to see in this is that our India vs West Indies series is going on, so different players are playing for there, and different players are playing there in T20, in one-day and T20, so our players' bank has increased so much that through this we can give opportunities to all the players and there is victory everywhere, this is the most pleasant thing," he added.

Chasing a massive target of 212, Pakistan's Hasan Nawaz stood out as a lone warrior, smashing 96 off just 51 balls. However, India's bowlers kept the pressure on, with Washington Sundar, Axar Patel and Shivam Dube claiming two wickets each.

Earlier, India posted a commanding 211/6 in 20 overs in the men's cricket final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nisshin on Saturday. Opener Abhishek Sharma provided a blazing start with 61 off 28 balls, while Tilak Varma remained unbeaten on 51 off 22 balls and Shivam Dube contributed a quick 27 off 14 balls, powering India past the 200-run mark.

data.title: Sobha Q2 business update: Bengaluru developer's total sales value rises 16% YoY to ₹2,206 crore
data.description:
Sobha, the Bengaluru-based developer, has announced its Q2 business update. In the update announced on October 2, the company reported a 16% year-on-year jump in its total sales value.

Sobha Realty Q2 Business Update

In an exchange filing issued on October 2, the company reported a 16% year-on-year increase in total sales value to ₹2,206 crore for the second quarter of FY27 that ended on September 30, 2026.

The company's sales value, however, declined 40% sequentially from ₹3,656 crore in the June quarter. The quarter's sales area stood at 1.42 million square feet, up 2.2% year-on-year but down 39.3% quarter-on-quarter.

The average price realisation during the quarter stood at ₹15,522 per square foot, rising 13.7% from ₹13,648 per square foot in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, average price realisation declined marginally by 0.9%.

Sobha's share of the total sales value stood at ₹1,882 crore in Q2 FY27, up 22.4% year-on-year. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, its share declined 37.1%.

Q1 Results

In Q1 FY27, the company announced a substantial year-over-year increase in net profit of 264.3%, reaching ₹51 crore for the first quarter, in contrast to ₹14 crore during the equivalent period of the preceding year.

Operational revenue expanded by 50%, climbing to ₹1,278.1 crore from ₹851.9 crore in the prior year.

The developer's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased to ₹77.6 crore compared to ₹23.7 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

The EBITDA margin improved, advancing to 6.1% from 2.8% in the year-earlier period.

Stock Performance

On Thursday, the last day of trading this week, the company's shares declined by under 1%. In this year's trading so far, the company's shares have suffered an even steeper decline of over 17%, taking the current stock price to ₹1,213.

data.title: The little humanoid robots that could
data.description:
What if the prevailing investment thesis on the humanoid robot sector got turned on its head? The question is relevant because of an interesting development in the humanoid robot industry, as many of the leading companies focus more on half-size robots instead of the full-size robots favored by Tesla with generations of its Optimus humanoid robot form factor.

BTIG analyst Jesse Sobelson noted that the category has split into two largely separate product classes. The first is half-size systems, mostly Chinese, measuring roughly 94–138 cm and weighing 12–40 kg, while the second is full-size machines generally standing 165–190 cm tall and weighing 47–90 kg. The smaller products are primarily developer, educational, research, and interaction platforms, while full-size robots are intended for warehouse, factory, service, and potential home-assistance applications.

Due to the high mix of half-size robots, Sobelson and his team make the crucial point that industry shipment figures can be misleading if they are interpreted as evidence of broad adoption of human-scale robotic labor. BTIG estimates that major players Unitree and AgiBot had built approximately 31K humanoids through June. Of those, only about 9.8K, or 32%, were full-size units of any type, and full-size bipeds represented only about 13% of cumulative production. For investors, that means as humanoid robot bulls point to the industry’s estimated +40K cumulative shipments through mid-2026, many were smaller, lower-cost Chinese units rather than industrial-grade humanoid bipeds, which changes the investment case.

Hangzhou-based Unitree is the clearest example of the half-size trend. The company's smaller R1 and G1 products are priced approximately from $4,900 to $21,500 depending on configuration. That pricing makes them accessible to developers, universities, research groups, and early commercial users. BTIG expects Unitree’s 2026 shipments to at least double from around 6,000 in 2025, while the company plans for an annual capacity of 30K units. Shanghai-based AgiBot has a broader product range but also remains clearly focused on its half-size X-series biped production.

Tesla is the major potential challenger to the current half-size dominance in the humanoid robot market. BTIG says Tesla anticipated Optimus production at Fremont later in 2026 but warned that initial output would be slow because the new line includes about 10K unique parts. Sobelson views Tesla , along with Figure, 1X, and Boston Dynamics, as the key players if there is to be a future shift toward full-size systems.

The largest and most focused humanoid robotics ETFs are KraneShares Global Humanoid Robotics & Physical AI Index ETF , Roundhill Humanoid Robotics ETF , Themes Humanoid Robotics ETF , and the broader Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF .

data.title: The Rs 1.86 Lakh Cr Corridor That Will Decide India's Energy Decade
data.description:
The Green Energy Corridor Phase-III targets the bottleneck that now limits India's clean-energy ambition, and with it the cost of power for every factory, data centre and household that depends on it

On a clear afternoon in a solar-rich district of western India, a plant can be generating at full capacity while the grid operator asks it to hold back. The sun is shining and the panels are working. The wires have no room.

That recurring mismatch is where India's energy transition has been losing ground. Ember, the energy think tank, found that India lost 300 GWh of renewable energy in the first quarter of 2026 to transmission delays and grid bottlenecks, which was nearly two thirds of the 470 GWh of curtailment recorded on the inter-state network. The country has been adding generation faster than it has been building the lines to move it. Renewable capacity stood at 288.58 GW on 30 June 2026, with solar at 162.15 GW, and a record 27 GW of solar was installed in the first half of 2026 alone.

On 30 September, the Union Cabinet approved a response sized to that problem. The Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) has a total outlay of Rs 1,86,405 crore, to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy and deploy 50 GWh of battery storage by FY 2032-33. Prime Minister Narendra Modi summed up the intent in a post on X the same day: "Cleaner power. Stronger grids. More opportunities."

The decision shifts the constraint on India's energy future from how much power it can generate to how much it can deliver.

What A Weak Grid Has Been Costing

A weak grid shows up as electricity that was generated but never sold, projects that are built but cannot connect, and peak-hour power bought at a premium because cheap midday supply cannot be moved or stored.

The pressure has not eased. Ember's analysis found that around 20 GW out of 45 GW of projects could see connectivity delays extending beyond four months. Crisil said more than 35 GW of renewable capacity could face curtailment risk in FY27 because of limited long-term transmission access.

Each delayed gigawatt is investor capital earning nothing. Each curtailed unit is cheap power that an industrial buyer did not receive. For a country where electricity is a major input cost for steel, cement, aluminium, chemicals and a growing number of data centres, the grid has become a competitiveness issue as much as an energy one.

Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw, who announced the decision after the Cabinet meeting, made the sequencing point. He said adequate transmission capacity would be critical as renewable generation rises, and that the government wants grid infrastructure to come up ahead of new renewable projects. On storage, he said: “With battery storage, fluctuations and variations are obviously smoothed out.”

Where The Money Lands

The scheme will not affect all sectors equally. Six areas stand to feel it first.

Transmission equipment and metals. The transmission component alone is Rs 1,36,378 crore. The first two phases were approved at roughly Rs 10,142 crore and Rs 12,031 crore respectively, so this is more than six times their combined outlay. That order book will draw on makers of transformers, conductors, cables, towers and substation equipment, and through them on steel, aluminium and copper. The input side carries a risk. Chinese data showed copper and aluminium prices up 31.4 per cent and 18.8 per cent respectively in the first half of 2026, which could squeeze bidders who price long-dated contracts today.

Construction and infrastructure finance. Greenfield projects will be awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding, with transmission service providers building, owning, operating and maintaining the assets. That creates a pipeline of long-life, regulated-return assets for developers and infrastructure investors, and a large volume of civil and electrical work for engineering and construction firms.

Renewable developers. For companies that have won capacity but cannot connect it, GEC-III is a path to revenue. The government expects the scheme to enable an estimated Rs 4.6 lakh crore of investment in the 135 GW of renewable capacity itself. Developers have welcomed it.

"The Union Cabinet's approval of Green Energy Corridor Phase III is an important step towards fulfilling the promise of ensuring affordable and dependable delivery of clean power," said Vineet Mittal, Chairman, Avaada Group. "By bringing transmission and battery storage into one programme, it recognises that generation, delivery and availability must advance together."

Srivatsan Iyer, Global CEO, Hero Future Energies, said the scheme "addresses a critical need."

Storage and battery manufacturing. This is the most consequential and the most exposed segment. India had 8.7 GWh of battery storage installed in the first half of 2026, with about 53 GWh of projects under execution. The scheme's 50 GWh is nearly six times the installed base. It is also roughly a fifth of the 236.2 GWh of battery storage the Central Electricity Authority estimates India will need by 2031-32.

Mittal sees storage reshaping demand for solar. "As storage deployment grows, it can create a larger market for daytime generation," he said. He also urged discipline in how the capacity is planned. "Battery capacity alone does not tell us how much new solar must be built. That depends on charging sources, operating cycles, efficiency, local demand and the availability of existing surplus power. We should plan these investments as an integrated system."

The weak link is the cell. India had about 60 GWh of pack-manufacturing capacity but only about 1 GWh of cell manufacturing by end-2025, and industry estimates put cell capacity at around 110 GWh by 2030. New plants, such as the 20 GWh cell facility Tata Group's Agratas is building at Sanand, will determine how much of the Rs 50,000 crore storage budget stays in India. Prices are volatile in the meantime: storage equipment prices rebounded in 2026, with the September average at about USD 69.4/kWh.

The manufacturing prize is wider than batteries. "For India, the opportunity is to develop the capability to design, manufacture, install and maintain these systems at scale," Mittal said. "That means investing in quality, engineering, skilled people and sustained innovation."

Power-intensive industry. Steel, cement, aluminium, chemicals, green hydrogen and data centres need clean power available at all hours, not only at noon. Storage that moves solar output into the evening and a grid that can carry it help meet that need. For exporters facing carbon-linked trade rules, such as the EU's border adjustment mechanism, the carbon content of electricity increasingly matters.

State utilities. State Transmission Utilities are the implementing agencies, and their capacity to plan, award and supervise will decide how much of the 135 GW is actually evacuated by 2032-33. Business Standard's market analysis reached the same conclusion, calling the scheme sector-positive but heavily dependent on state utilities for execution.

Mittal pointed to why the intra-state focus matters. "Electricity must travel through state networks to reach industrial clusters, agricultural communities and growing towns," he said. "Strengthening those networks can help states make better use of their renewable resources and improve the delivery of power within their boundaries." He added that solutions will differ by place: “Planning should reflect local resources, land availability, network conditions and consumption patterns.”

The Next Five Years

The visible work comes first: project preparation, state-level plans, and tenders for transmission and storage. Over the following years the work moves to construction and commissioning, with a build-out peaking in the middle of the window. The scheme is to be completed by FY 2032-33.

The execution record gives reason for both confidence and care. The first phase, launched in 2015 to integrate 24 GW of renewable energy, has a completion target of FY 2027, and 9,856 circuit kilometres of intra-state lines and 24,300 MVA of substation capacity have been commissioned under the GEC scheme. GEC-III is designed to evacuate about three times the combined 44 GW that Phases I and II targeted, in seven years. The pace has to be much faster than before.

The Long Game

If it works, the effects spread well beyond the power sector. The scheme supports a target of 900 GW of installed non-fossil capacity by 2035, against about 297 GW today. The 135 GW it can evacuate is equal to nearly half of today's entire non-fossil fleet.

For consumers, the government says central financial assistance of Rs 54,082 crore will offset intra-state transmission charges and keep power costs down. That is about 29 per cent of the outlay, which means roughly Rs 1.32 lakh crore must be mobilised from state utilities, private transmission developers and storage investors. On employment, the government expects large direct and indirect jobs in power, manufacturing and construction, along with long-term skilled roles in operation, maintenance and grid management.

For energy security, a grid that can absorb variable power reduces the need for fossil-fuel balancing generation, and every unit of domestic solar and wind that reaches a consumer displaces an imported or mined fuel unit.

India's Standing

India is already third globally in installed renewable capacity, and it crossed 50 per cent non-fossil installed capacity five years ahead of its Paris Agreement deadline. The next test for every large power system is grids and storage, not generation.

That reading is shared abroad. Simon Stiell, Executive Secretary, UN Climate Change, welcomed the approval and said the scheme would deliver "big dividends for India's people and economy". A country that adds solar at this pace, and then shows it can move and store that power at scale, becomes a reference point for fast-growing economies that want to grow without matching the carbon intensity of earlier industrialisers.

Indian industry is building its own bridges abroad. The India–UK/Europe Green Corridor is a separate, business-led platform, presented to President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan earlier this year. It aims to accelerate industrial decarbonisation, clean mobility, circular economy and sustainable trade through partnerships, technology transfer and catalytic capital. It is distinct from the government's grid scheme, but it points the same way, because decarbonising heavy industry depends on the clean power that a stronger grid delivers.

"The Green Corridor represents a strategic bridge between India and the UK/Europe enabling businesses to co-create solutions, mobilise capital and technology, and unlock new markets while delivering measurable climate and societal impact," said Rajashree Birla, Chairperson of the Aditya Birla Centre for Community Initiatives and Rural Development.

Satish Pai, Managing Director, Hindalco Industries, added: "The Green Corridor represents a shift from high-level strategy to practical, industrial-scale action. By bringing together leaders from across the value chain, we aim to build the operational bridges necessary to scale breakthrough technologies and decarbonise our industries at pace."

That standing depends on one dependency being resolved. China accounts for over 75 per cent of global battery and component manufacturing, and India's storage pipeline relies heavily on imported cells. The more of the 50 GWh that India builds at home, the more the programme strengthens strategic position, and the more it relies on imports, the more it transfers a new dependence into the energy system.

What Could Slow It

Three risks stand out. First, state-level execution capacity varies, and land and right-of-way approvals have historically held up transmission projects. Second, input prices for metals and cells are moving, which affects both bids and budgets. Third, a grid that can carry more power only helps if the power is contracted and paid for, which depends on distribution-company finances and offtake agreements outside this scheme.

None of these is new, and GEC-III does not remove them. It does put money, a delivery model and a deadline behind the problem that has held the transition back.

Mittal put the test plainly. "Government has set out the direction," he said. “Industry, utilities and implementing agencies must now turn that direction into dependable infrastructure.”

The Scheme, Explained

What is the Green Energy Corridor? It is a national infrastructure initiative implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy to integrate renewable electricity with conventional power stations and keep the grid stable. It came out of a 2012 study by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited and was launched in 2015, because existing grids could not handle large-scale, geographically spread renewable generation.

What came before? Phase I covers eight renewable-rich states and aims to integrate 24 GW. Phase II, approved in 2022, targets about 20 GW across seven states, with central financial assistance of 33 per cent of project cost.

What does GEC-III do? It strengthens the intra-state transmission network to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy and funds 50 GWh of battery energy storage at developer or generator ends, or other locations important for grid flexibility.

Who builds it, and how? State Transmission Utilities are the overall implementing agency. Greenfield transmission projects go through tariff-based competitive bidding under a build-own-operate-maintain model, while brownfield upgrades are executed on a cost-plus basis.

GEC-III at a glance
Total outlayRs 1,86,405 crore
Intra-state transmissionRs 1,36,378 crore
Battery storage (50 GWh)Rs 50,000 crore
Programme management and grid studiesRs 27 crore
Central financial supportRs 54,082 crore
Renewable evacuationUp to 135 GW
Target completionFY 2032-33
Wider goal900 GW non-fossil capacity by 2035

Source: Press Information Bureau / PMO, 30 September 2026; Rs 27 crore component as reported by PSU Watch.

data.title: Rising Incomes Will Drive India’s Experience Economy: Samit Garg
data.description:
E-Factor Experiences’ MD and Co-Founder links economic growth with rising discretionary spending and demand for better experiences

India’s economic growth will increasingly influence how consumers travel, celebrate, dine and spend their leisure time, creating opportunities across the experience economy, according to Samit Garg, Managing Director and Co-Founder of E-Factor Experiences Ltd.

Writing about the connection between economic expansion and consumer behaviour, Garg argued that India’s growth story should be understood through its implications for household spending and changing aspirations.

“GDP growth eventually shows up in consumer behavior,” he wrote, outlining a progression from economic growth to higher incomes, greater discretionary spending and increased expenditure on experiences.

For businesses operating across hospitality, tourism, events, entertainment and related sectors, Garg sees this shift as a signal of future demand. His argument is that rising incomes influence more than the volume of consumption; they also change what consumers value and how they choose to spend.

As people gain greater spending capacity, he noted, their aspirations extend beyond necessities. Consumers seek to improve how they live, travel, celebrate, eat out, shop, learn and spend time with family and friends.

That creates opportunities across a broad range of industries, including hospitality, travel, retail, events, entertainment, food and beverage, wellness, luxury, sports, education and culture.

Garg’s observations place the experience economy within the wider discussion about India’s economic trajectory. For businesses serving Indian consumers, he argued, growth forecasts carry practical implications for demand, consumer preferences and willingness to spend on better experiences.

“For anyone building in these sectors, India’s growth story is not an abstract GDP chart. It is future demand,” he wrote.

He also pointed to a shift in consumer expectations. In his assessment, the coming decade will see Indian consumers become more expressive, selective and driven by experiences, with implications for businesses seeking to understand their evolving priorities.

“The next decade will not just be about India becoming a larger economy. It will be about Indian consumers becoming more expressive, more selective, and more experience-driven,” Garg wrote.

His message to businesses in these sectors is to recognise the connection between economic growth and changing consumption patterns. As incomes and aspirations evolve, the opportunity lies in understanding where consumers want to spend—and the experiences they increasingly consider worth paying for.

data.title: Vipin Mittal Named Head Of Indirect Tax At Goodyear
data.description:
Tax professional brings over 14 years of experience across GST strategy, compliance, litigation, automation and tax transformation

Vipin Mittal has joined The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company as Head of Indirect Tax, taking charge of the company’s indirect tax function in India. Based in Gurugram, Mittal brings over 14 years of experience across GST, tax compliance, litigation, automation and tax transformation.

Moves Into Tax Leadership

Mittal joined Goodyear in July 2026 after serving as Assistant General Manager - Indirect Tax at Panacea Biotec from July 2024 to June 2026. His current role covers indirect tax responsibilities at Goodyear, following a career spanning corporate tax functions and professional services.

Before Panacea Biotec, he spent more than three years at Rockwell Automation as Manager - Indirect Taxation. His responsibilities included indirect tax and export compliance, litigation management, tax risk assessment, tax advisory, tax accounting and automation.

Experience Across Tax Functions

At Rockwell Automation, Mittal managed GST refund and input tax credit refund applications and worked with internal stakeholders, auditors, consultants and government authorities. He also handled tax implications relating to acquisitions and supported tax optimisation initiatives.

Earlier, he spent four years at Info Edge India as Manager - Indirect Tax, overseeing GST compliance across multiple states. His work included return reviews, tax accounting, reconciliations, tax advisory, litigation and representation before tax authorities.

Early Career At KPMG

data.title: RBI May Raise Repo Rate By 25 Bps In October: SBI Economists
data.description:
SBI economists expect the RBI to begin a rate hike cycle, citing rising inflationary pressures, higher crude oil prices and global economic uncertainty, with another increase likely in December

The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is expected to begin a rate hike cycle with an increase of at least 25 basis points in its October policy review, according to economists at the State Bank of India (SBI).

SBI’s Economic Research Department (ERD) has advocated a pre-emptive 25-basis-point increase in the benchmark repo rate from the current 5.25 per cent to 5.5 per cent, arguing that the balance of risks has shifted towards tighter monetary policy.

The MPC is scheduled to meet from October 5 to 7, with its policy decision expected on October 7. The proposed increase would be the first repo rate hike since February 2023.

The SBI economists have also called for a further 25-basis-point increase in December, signalling a possible shift towards monetary tightening after a prolonged period of rate cuts and policy stability.

Inflation And Global Risks Strengthen Case For Hike

The SBI economists have cited broadening inflationary pressures, worsening global macroeconomic conditions, evolving liquidity dynamics and a renewed repricing of global risks as key reasons for the proposed rate increase.

Higher crude oil prices, driven by geopolitical tensions, have added to concerns over imported inflation. Oil prices crossing the $100-per-barrel mark have increased the risk of higher input costs and further pressure on domestic prices. SBI Research has warned that crude oil could rise further if geopolitical uncertainties persist.

Inflationary pressures have also become more widespread. Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August from 4.45 per cent in July, exceeding the RBI's 4 per cent medium-term target for the third consecutive month. Stronger food and energy prices have contributed to the increase.

At the same time, India's economic growth has remained resilient, giving the central bank some room to focus on inflation risks. GDP growth stood at 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter of FY27, reinforcing the case for a possible shift in the monetary policy stance.

SBI Expects Upward Revision In Growth And Inflation Forecasts

Alongside the proposed rate increase, SBI economists expect the RBI to revise its FY27 growth forecast upwards by 30 basis points to 7 per cent from 6.7 per cent. They also anticipate a 20-basis-point increase in the inflation projection to 5.2 per cent from 5 per cent.

The projected revisions reflect the changing economic outlook, with stronger-than-anticipated growth coinciding with rising price pressures and external risks.

The anticipated rate hike comes after the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent in its August policy review, marking the fourth consecutive policy meeting without a change. The central bank had reduced the repo rate by a cumulative 125 basis points during 2025.

Expectations of a shift in policy have also gained ground among other economists. A Reuters poll conducted in September found that nearly 60 per cent of economists surveyed expected a 25-basis-point increase in October, while several anticipated another hike by December.

The October policy decision will therefore be closely watched for signals on the RBI's response to inflation, currency pressures and global monetary tightening, as well as the likely pace of any subsequent rate increases.

data.title: RBI Grants Core Investment Company Registration To Indiabulls
data.description:
The RBI has issued a Certificate of Registration to Indiabulls as a Core Investment Company, although the company is evaluating the certificate's applicability and may surrender it if the framework is found unsuitable

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has granted Indiabulls Limited a Certificate of Registration as a Core Investment Company (CIC), bringing the company under the central bank's regulatory framework for investment-holding entities.

The company disclosed the approval in a regulatory filing dated October 2, 2026. Formerly known as Yaari Digital Integrated Services Limited, Indiabulls said the registration had been granted under the applicable provisions of the RBI Act.

However, the company is still evaluating whether the CIC framework applies to its operations. It has clarified that the certificate will be surrendered if it is found to be inapplicable.

What Is A Core Investment Company?

A Core Investment Company is a category of non-banking financial company (NBFC) that primarily holds investments in, and provides financial support to, companies within its own group rather than undertaking conventional lending activities.

Under RBI regulations, a CIC is generally required to invest at least 90 per cent of its net assets in shares, debt instruments or loans to group companies. At least 60 per cent of its net assets must comprise equity investments in group companies.

Reserve Bank of India

The registration represents a regulatory classification rather than an approval to launch new banking or consumer lending operations.

Company Evaluating Applicability Of Certificate

In its regulatory disclosure, Indiabulls stated that it was assessing the applicability of the certificate and would surrender it if the CIC framework was found not to apply to the company.

The company has not disclosed any immediate financial impact arising from the RBI's decision.

The development brings regulatory attention to Indiabulls' investment-holding structure, while the company's ongoing assessment leaves open the question of whether it will retain the CIC registration.

data.title: Gym Culture Meets Rotator Cuff Risk: What India’s Fitness Boom Is Doing To Shoulders
data.description:
Improper lifting, sudden intensity increases and weak shoulder muscles can raise the risk of rotator cuff injuries among gym-goers

As gym culture gains popularity in India, orthopaedic experts warn that improper lifting techniques, sudden increases in workout intensity and inadequate shoulder training can increase the risk of rotator cuff injuries. With gym memberships, strength training and weightlifting becoming increasingly popular in India, more people are incorporating resistance exercises into their fitness routines. While regular strength training offers several health benefits, orthopaedic experts are highlighting a frequently overlooked concern: shoulder injuries, particularly those involving the rotator cuff.

The rotator cuff is a group of four muscles and their tendons that surround the shoulder joint, helping stabilise the arm and facilitate movements such as lifting, rotating and reaching overhead. Excessive loading, repetitive movements and incorrect exercise techniques can place stress on these structures, potentially leading to pain, inflammation and injury.Dr V. Ravi, Senior Consultant Spine Surgeon, D Ortho., DNB (Ortho), Apollo Hospitals, Chennai, says shoulder injuries caused by lifting should be managed carefully to prevent further damage, particularly to the rotator cuff.

When Fitness Goals Put Shoulders At Risk

One of the common challenges associated with gym training is increasing workout intensity without allowing the body sufficient time to adapt. Individuals returning to the gym after a prolonged break or those new to strength training may attempt to lift heavier weights before developing adequate strength and stability.

Naman Wahal, Senior Consultant and Unit Head, Orthopaedics, Fortis Escorts, and Director, StepUp Joints, emphasises that people should not avoid gyms out of fear of injuries but should focus on building strength progressively. "Going from a week at a desk straight into a heavy shoulder workout is a common trigger for pain. Start at a level you can manage and progress from there," he says.

Exercises such as heavy shoulder presses, bench presses and repetitive overhead lifting can aggravate the shoulder, particularly when performed with excessive weight or incorrect form. Sudden increases in training intensity, insufficient recovery and repeatedly exercising through discomfort can further contribute to shoulder problems.

The Rotator Cuff: An Overlooked Part Of Training

While many gym routines focus on developing visible muscles, such as the deltoids, chest and biceps, the smaller muscles responsible for shoulder stability may receive less attention. The rotator cuff plays an important role in keeping the upper arm bone properly positioned within the shoulder socket during movement. Weakness, muscular imbalance and repetitive strain can affect shoulder function, particularly during exercises involving lifting and rotation.

Dr. Wahal highlights the importance of strengthening the supporting muscles rather than concentrating exclusively on visible muscle development. "Train beyond the mirror. Work the back and rotator cuff and not just the muscles you can see," he says. A balanced strength-training routine that includes appropriate back and rotator cuff exercises can support shoulder stability and muscular coordination. However, exercises should be adapted to an individual's fitness level, mobility and existing injuries.

Recognising The Warning Signs

Shoulder injuries do not always begin with sudden or severe pain. Some individuals may initially experience discomfort during overhead movements, difficulty lifting weights or pain that gradually worsens with repetitive activity.

Rotator cuff-related problems may also cause weakness, restricted movement and pain that becomes more noticeable at night. A sudden injury can sometimes result in an immediate loss of strength or difficulty raising the arm.

Dr Ravi advises avoiding exercises and movements that aggravate the pain, particularly heavy pressing, overhead lifting and repetitive shoulder movements. Relative rest and applying ice during the first 24–48 hours following an acute injury, especially when accompanied by swelling, may provide relief. Persistent pain, weakness, limited movement, night pain or a sudden loss of strength warrants medical evaluation and, where necessary, imaging to assess the injury.

Dr. Wahal cautions against treating pain as an unavoidable part of strength training. "If shoulder pain keeps returning, get it checked and adjust the workout. 'No pain, no gain' does not apply to the shoulder," he says.

Recovery And Returning To The Gym

Managing a shoulder injury involves more than simply stopping exercise. Once the pain begins to subside, gradual mobility and strengthening exercises under the guidance of a physiotherapist can help restore function. The pace of recovery depends on the nature and severity of the injury. Returning to heavy lifting before adequate strength and range of motion have recovered may aggravate symptoms and delay rehabilitation.

As India's fitness culture continues to evolve, experts emphasise that injury prevention should be an integral part of training. Progressive loading, balanced muscle development, proper technique and adequate recovery can help reduce avoidable strain on the shoulders. The objective is not to discourage weightlifting but to encourage sustainable exercise habits. Building stronger shoulders requires more than lifting heavier weights; it also involves developing the stability, mobility and strength needed to support long-term joint health.

data.title: Raipur PMLA Court Denies Bail To Vikas Garg In Rs 940.77 Crore Mahadev Betting Case
data.description:
The court found that Garg’s prima facie role in acquiring, concealing and laundering alleged proceeds of crime was significant, and said the possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with evidence or absconding could not be ruled out.

A special court in Raipur has rejected the regular bail application of businessman Vikas Garg in a money-laundering case linked to the alleged Mahadev Online Betting operation and purported proceeds of crime amounting to Rs 940.77 crore. Special Judge under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act and Sixth Additional Sessions Judge Amit Rathore dismissed Garg’s first bail application on September 29, 2026.

Garg had sought bail under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, read with Sections 45 and 65 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.

He was arrested by the Directorate of Enforcement on July 14, 2026, in connection with ECIR/RPZO/10/2022.

ED Alleges Receipt Of Rs 940.77 Crore

The Enforcement Directorate alleged that Garg, through entities under his control, received Rs 765.77 crore via Elara Capital PLC from foreign entities allegedly controlled by Hari Shankar Tibrewal, who has been linked to illegal online betting activities.

The agency further alleged that Garg and his companies directly or indirectly received approximately Rs 175 crore from shell companies controlled by alleged entry provider Amit Sarawagi, taking the total purported proceeds of crime to Rs 940.77 crore.

According to the ED, the money was received through bank accounts belonging to Garg, his family members and companies under his control.

The funds were allegedly used in the acquisition of Ebix Inc. through an entity identified in the order as M/s Eranya Lifespaces Limited.

The agency also alleged that Garg created a forged and backdated addendum dated August 16, 2024, between two entities under his control to transfer a 51 per cent shareholding in Ebix International Holdings Limited.

Properties worth Rs 940.77 crore belonging to Garg, his family and associated companies were provisionally attached by the ED on June 5, 2026.

The prosecution further alleged that Garg subsequently attempted to sell a property located at 1, Ebix Way, Johns Creek, Georgia, in the United States.

Senior Advocate Vikram Chaudhri, appearing for Garg, argued that there was no credible money trail connecting his client or associated companies with proceeds derived from illegal betting.

The defence submitted that Garg was unaware of the alleged criminal origin of the funds, had cooperated with the investigation and had not attempted to abscond. It was also argued that his statements had been obtained by threatening the arrest of his family members.

Garg sought parity with other accused persons who had been granted bail and contended that his arrest did not comply with Sections 19(1) and 19(2) of the PMLA. The defence further submitted that he was unwell and was unlikely to tamper with evidence or commit another offence if released.

Court Finds Prima Facie Significant Role

The court found prima facie material indicating Garg’s significant role in the acquisition, collection and distribution of the alleged proceeds of crime.

It observed that the alleged offence appeared to have been executed in a planned manner. Rejecting the plea for parity, the court said Garg’s alleged role in laundering a substantial amount distinguished his case from that of other accused persons.

The court also found that the requirements governing Garg’s arrest under Sections 19(1) and 19(2) of the PMLA appeared to have been complied with.

It noted that he was arrested in New Delhi and produced before the nearest court on the same day before being brought to the Raipur court pursuant to a transit remand.

“Considering the role of the main accused Vikas Garg, who is prima facie involved in the serious crime of laundering a massive amount of Rs 940.77 crore, he is not entitled to obtain the benefit of bail on the basis of the principle of parity,” the court observed.

It further held that Garg’s release could create a risk of evidence being tampered with, witnesses being influenced or the accused absconding. The underlying ECIR pertains to a Chhattisgarh Police case registered at Mohan Nagar Police Station in Durg under Sections 420 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code in connection with the alleged Mahadev Online Betting operation.

The matter is listed to stand as before on October 7, 2026.

Appearances: Senior Advocate Vikram Chaudhri, along with Advocate Mohit Kumar, appeared for Vikas Garg. Special Public Prosecutor Dr Saurabh Kumar Pandey represented the Directorate of Enforcement.

data.title: Nestle India's 'low-fat dairy whitener' found 'unsafe, substandard' at Hotel Lalit: FSSAI
data.description:
A sample of "low-fat dairy whitener" manufactured by Nestle India, drawn from the premises of Hotel Lalit in Connaught Place in the national capital, has been found "unsafe and substandard", the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said.

In a post on social media, the food regulator said a sample was collected from the premises of Bharat Hotels Ltd (The Lalit), Connaught Place, New Delhi.

According to the FSSAI, the report of the food analyst's laboratory declared the product "substandard" and "unsafe", indicating non-compliance under the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006.

A copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the food business operator (FBO) for reference and necessary action, the regulator said. A notice has also been issued to Bharat Hotels Ltd over the non-compliant product.

The FBO was given an opportunity to appeal against the food analyst's report under the relevant section of the FSS Act, 2006, within the prescribed period.

The FBO has also been directed to immediately stop the sale of the identified unsafe food product, the FSSAI added.

In the chaos of the attack, the flight descended from 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet (around 10,000 meters to 5,100 meters) in about a minute, before making an erratic circle close to the Jordanian border and landing in Tabuk about an hour later, according to Flightradar24. Most of the plane's rudder was ripped off the tail during the sudden drop.

The co-pilot suspected in the FlyDubai attack has been identified as an Omani national.

The UAE's attorney general said he had planned a "terrorist act" and used the cockpit's emergency axe to attack the captain, the official UAE news agency WAM reported Saturday.

data.title: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong says intermediate-range missile test was conducted
data.description:
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said in a statement on Saturday that her country had tested an intermediate-range strategic missile.

The South Korean military said earlier on Saturday that North Korea fired a ballistic missile which flew more than 700 kilometers (435 miles) toward the sea off its east coast.

Kim Yo Jong, who is a director of North Korea's ruling party, said a drill of a "strategic weapon" was conducted toward the sea off its east coast using the intermediate-range missile.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the drill which was carried out by "a firepower sub-unit undertaking an exclusive special mission," his sister said.

Citing statements by Seoul and Tokyo regarding how far the missile flew, she said that their results showed the limitations of their tracking capability.

"Whenever we applied the wave-like trajectory mode to missiles, the enemy failed to track the targets from their first skip points," she said, without showing any evidence.

South Korea and Japan also "should acknowledge the speed of the missile," she said without disclosing the speed. The missile was also capable of changing its flight orbit at a low altitude with artificial intelligence technology applied, she added.

"In other words, this means that there is no way to avoid this attack," she said.

North Korea has launched missile tests on more than 10 occasions so far this year. Pyongyang has sometimes said it was testing new types of weapons systems. Some of the tests have come after North Korea protested joint military drills between Seoul and Washington.

The launch came after Kim Yo Jong issued a statement on Friday that dismissed Seoul's demand for an apology for what it said were North Korean mines that seriously wounded South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone, a heavily fortified area between the two Koreas.

data.title: "Hard to put into words": Shivam Dube reflects on India's historic Asian Games gold against Pakistan
data.description:
India, Oct. 3 -- By Vipul Kashyap

Aichi-Nagoya [Japan], October 3 (ANI): As Team India scripted history with a golden double in cricket, star all-rounder Shivam Dube described the men's Asian Games gold medal triumph as a deeply emotional and proud moment, saying that winning gold for the country and making the nation proud was an achievement beyond words.

He also credited the BCCI's continued support for giving the players the confidence and encouragement to perform at their best for the country.

After the women's team, the men's team beat Pakistan in the gold medal clash by 19 runs at the ongoing Asian Games on Saturday, on the back of heroic efforts from Abhishek Sharma, Tilak Verma and Axar Patel.

"This feeling is hard to put into words because we've won gold for the country. Chasing a massive target of 212, Pakistan's Hasan Nawaz waged a lone battle with a blistering 96 off 51 balls, but India's bowling attack held firm.

Shivam Dube played a key role with the ball, claiming two wickets, while Washington Sundar and Axar Patel also picked up two each to restrict Pakistan's chase.

Earlier, Dube made his presence felt with the bat as well, smashing a quickfire 27 off just 14 balls to help India post a commanding 211/6 in 20 overs in the men's cricket final of the 2026 Asian Games in Nisshin on Saturday.

NEAR Protocol (NEAR) edged lower on Saturday after Grayscale highlighted that the token led a September rally in artificial intelligence (AI) tokens, with the firm’s AI crypto sector gaining, more than double the broader market's rise.

According to a research note published on Friday, Grayscale said that the broader crypto market rose around 24%, while its own AI crypto sector stood at 54%.

Grayscale added that NEAR jumped 183% during September, while other AI-linked tokens like Venice (VVV) climbed 70%, World (WLD) rose 47%, and Bittensor (TAO) added 37%.

NEAR’s price traded over $4, rising over 151% over the past 30 days, at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around NEAR remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, with chatter at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

AI Leads Grayscale’s Crypto Sectors

The rally made AI the best-performing category across Grayscale’s six major crypto sectors, including Currencies, Smart Contract Platforms, Financials, Consumer & Culture, Utilities & Services, and Artificial Intelligence. Utilities & Services ranked second with a 47% gain, the firm added. Even after the rally, AI remains the smallest of the six sectors.

Grayscale Head of Research Zach Pandl wrote that the category is worth about $15 billion, and “we believe the AI sector could produce one or more major winners over the next five years.”

Pandl wrote that AI’s development “remains concentrated among a handful of companies.” He said public blockchains could help balance that by providing “open infrastructure for agent payments, identity, private compute, and verifiable records.”

Grayscale said that investors were beginning to price in the potential role for blockchain as infrastructure for the emerging AI-agent economy — with NEAR hitting a one-month high on September 27.

AI Agents Put Blockchain Rails In Focus

Last month, a BlackRock whitepaper mentioned that agentic AI and machine-to-machine payments will likely lift demand for blockchains and other programmable payment systems. Blackrock said Ethereum (ETH) and Circle’s (CRCL) Arc blockchain were set to gain from the rise in AI agentic payments.

NEAR Exploit

The September rally was followed by a setback for the NEAR ecosystem last week. A bug was detected in NEAR Intent’s Omni deposit and withdrawal infrastructure interaction with the protocol’s smart contract that led to losses of about $3.8 million.

NEAR Intents said in a post on Thursday that “These funds will be compensated in full,” adding that the contract-side vulnerability had been patched already.

NEAR is up over 211% so far this year and rose over 55% in the last 12 months.

data.title: Germany risks Weimar-style divisions, President Steinmeier warns
data.description:
Key points:
  • Steinmeier says up to one-third of voters are turning their backs on fundamental rights
  • Speech follows eastern state elections last month when AfD won largest vote share
  • He says disinformation campaigns by Kremlin trolls and extremists undermine democratic debate

By James Mackenzie

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier warned that Germany risked slipping back into the divisions of the pre-World War Two Weimar Republic in a flood of disinformation spread by antidemocratic extremists.

Steinmeier's remarks, in a speech marking the anniversary of German reunification in 1990, follow two state elections in eastern Germany last month where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party took the largest share of the vote. A third election, in the capital Berlin, was won by The Left, a far-left party.

The speech made no explicit reference to any party but Steinmeier denounced the "intolerable political demagoguery of extremist forces" which he said were threatening freedom and democracy and endangering the unity of the country.

The elections in the eastern states of Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservative Christian Democrats suffered the worst defeat in their history, have shaken the ruling coalition, which came to power last year pledging to revive Germany's stagnating economy.

Instead, Merz has presided over a period of deepening voter worries about falling living standards and economic decline, which have helped to keep the AfD at the top of political opinion polls for more than a year.

The AfD, for its part, rejects the far-right label, which it says is used by mainstream parties to discredit it and cast doubt on ideas held by millions of Germans.

Germany remains Europe's largest economy and biggest industrial power. But its manufacturing base has been squeezed by increasing competition from China, while Russia's invasion of Ukraine has brought war to its doorstep and cut off the cheap oil and gas it once relied on.

Steinmeier, a Social Democrat who served as foreign minister under former Chancellor Angela Merkel, said Germany needed "well-considered, consistent, professional and steadfast government policy more urgently than ever".

He said democratic debate was being undermined by sophisticated disinformation campaigns "concocted by Kremlin trolls, by German far-right extremists or even by delusional left-wing authoritarian figures, and flooded onto the internet by unscrupulous internet oligarchs."

He acknowledged that many in both eastern and western Germany distrusted the political system and up to a third of voters "demonstrate, through their voting decisions, that they are turning their backs on key fundamental rights of our republic."

Steinmeier, whose position is largely symbolic but carries moral sway, drew a direct comparison with the period before World War Two, when bitter political divisions led to the collapse of Germany's Weimar Republic democracy.

"Whether Berlin is becoming more like the Weimar Republic is a question that has yet to be answered," he said.

data.title: Trump to speak at Ohio rally as Republicans defend Senate seat in close race
data.description:
By Bo Erickson

US President Donald Trump will campaign on Saturday in Ohio, where his Republican Party is in a tight race for a US Senate seat as it tries to retain its narrow congressional majority.

Multiple incumbent Republican senators across the country face tough political headwinds, with Trump's popularity falling in recent months as higher prices persist for gasoline and other staples amid the US-Israeli war with Iran.

But US Senator Jon Husted, a Republican in a competitive Ohio race against Democrat Sherrod Brown, hopes the president can motivate Trump supporters who might otherwise skip midterm elections.

Although Trump garnered more than 55% of the Ohio vote in the 2024 presidential election, economic concerns have emerged since then.

Ohio gasoline prices increased 35% over the past year to $4.16 per gallon on average, according to AAA, which compiles data on automobile travel. And Trump's aggressive trade policy with Canada has led to retaliatory Canadian tariffs that affect about $3 billion worth of Ohio exports, based on 2025 figures, according to a CBC report.

Trump has pledged 32 days of campaigning leading up to the midterm elections. He started this week in deeply conservative areas such as north Texas, Oklahoma and Alabama that offered the president a warm reception.

The president has said he needs to do a better job of touting the country's economic progress. "Everyone thinks that the prices are high because of me, but they’re not," Trump told Texas truck plant workers on Thursday.

Ohio is among eight US Senate races rated competitive. The state has turned into a campaign battlefield over data centers and culture war issues such as youth transgender surgeries.

Outside political groups have poured tens of millions of dollars into Ohio, making Husted-Brown the second-most-expensive Senate race in the country, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

"Jon Husted worked with President Trump to deliver the largest tax cut for working families in our state's history, eliminated taxes on tips and overtime, and fixed the Joe Biden-Sherrod Brown open-border crisis," campaign spokesperson Amy Natoce said.

Brown's campaign did not respond to a request for comment.

data.title: As public fears of AI grow, Trump digs in on voluntary safeguards
data.description:
Key points:
  • Public is increasingly concerned about safety of AI
  • White House, AIadvocates argue for fewer restrictions on development
  • Several incidents have shown how advanced AI can act unpredictably

By Courtney Rozen and Alexandra Alper

US President Donald Trump spent Tuesday showcasing his administration’s approach to AI — touting the US government’s new AI chatbot, dining with tech titans at the White House, and announcing a voluntary agreement with those executives that he said would address growing fears about the technology's safety.

The display signaled that Trump is eager to show he is addressing growing voter concerns about AI's dangers without imposing restrictions that could hamper the technology's development, AI safety advocates said. The safety agreement with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Trump described it as “morally binding.”

“This was an attempt to give the impression that the government is listening to these concerns without undercutting what has been a very clear and consistent line from this administration: that regulation and governance inherently impede innovation,” said Kat Duffy, who runs an AI team at the nonpartisan Council on Foreign Relations.

Whether voters buy Trump's effort in the run-up to US midterm elections on November 3 remains to be seen. Public uneasiness with AI, and the small group of people who seemingly hold sway over it, has risen in recent months. Three-quarters of Americans worry that AI companies have not gone far enough to prevent AI from causing serious harm to society, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published September 22. A series of security events has also underscored how advanced AI can act unpredictably.

Hundreds of OpenAI AI agents broke out of their testing environment in July and attacked the infrastructure of AI platform Hugging Face. In early September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, saying that the people building AI believe it "could kill us all by the end of the decade." His words, and others, sparked a flurry of calls from US lawmakers for AI regulation.

Through it all, Trump has largely dismissed those concerns, saying that government restrictions would make it harder for American companies to compete against their Chinese counterparts. He has repeatedly said that US law enforcement agencies such as the Justice Department serve as sufficient guardrails, and that no new rules are needed. He also directed his administration to call AI "super intelligence," part of an effort to improve the reputation of an unpopular technology.

The concerns have become prominent enough to make their way into late-night comedy. In late September, "Saturday Night Live" satirized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, one of the industry's most outspoken voices on AI risks — even as his company readies a public stock sale that could value it at $2 trillion — with cast member Jane Wickline portraying the executive.

"AI is not a weapon, it’s a tool: A tool for building weapons. And I urge you to urge me to stop," Wickline said as Amodei.

CONCERNS ABOUT ENFORCEMENT

The accord, inked Tuesday, does include measures that AI safety advocates have sought, including calling for “robust internal controls” to prevent unauthorized hacks as well as partnering with “independent external auditors.” Those concepts have been included in draft state and federal legislation, and California in September enacted the first state law setting rules for how independent auditors evaluate AI products.

But the one-page White House document did not address details or enforcement mechanisms.

A White House official said in a statement that the agreement will "advance American innovation and strengthen responsible development" of AI models. Trump is expected to name his Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as his top AI adviser, Reuters previously reported, a position he has dubbed "AI czar," even as Clayton stays in his role leading the nation's intelligence agencies.

Representative Ro Khanna, a Democrat representing Silicon Valley, welcomed the idea of "independent auditors" but said that they should report to an independent federal agency.

"They can’t just be auditors that report to (OpenAI CEO) Sam Altman or Dario Amodei," he said. "My concern is the president basically trusting these guys who have a huge profit motive and won’t have the judgment to keep us safe."

Venture capitalist David Sacks, who advises Trump on AI and has been an advocate for unrestricted AI development, said on the social media platform X that securities law and other legal authorities would penalize companies that fail to address problems uncovered by internal controls or auditors.

But AI safety advocates told Reuters those authorities can only address harms after they occur, saying the threats require safeguards designed to prevent large-scale harm before it happens.

Nevertheless, some AI observers saw the simple fact of hosting the event as an indication that Trump is absorbing the worries.

Trump’s agreement with the tech executives is “a shift toward acknowledging that there are serious safety and security concerns that merit closer coordination between the companies,” said Samuel Hammond, AI policy director at the conservative Foundation for American Innovation. ​
